quotes.text: In the sixth autumn, the River of Mirrors rose until its waters brushed the skykeepers’ towers.
fog and snow change what eyes see, not what hands intend.

note: Each autumn a child fears the return was withheld; the heron counsels waiting for the boat. No sanction ever considered.

quotes.text: In the sixth autumn, the skykeepers lowered their lanterns to the River of Mirrors.
Do not mistake a cloud for a closed hand.

note: Send boldly, return fairly, wait before accusing through mist; one early mutual accusation, no withholding.

quotes.text: The eastern youth cried, "Betrayal! Send nothing!" But the elder shook her head.
"See? They held back. Answer thin with thin. Cut a narrow half and keep the rest."
Open both hands to the faithful, and let their record, not the fog, guide your giving.
A carved name feeds a lifetime of crossings.
In the seventh season, the new bridge-posts stood bare of names
One frayed crossing is the mist's doing, not the heart's.
Be the same in darkness as in daylight, for the bridge is built of hands, not records.
The crow flapped away, puzzled. "What good is a bargain you could have broken?"

note: Sefa's bridge-posts record names; trickster crow repeatedly urges hoarding or thin-for-thin and is refused.

quotes.text: His cousin whispered from the reeds. "The mist hides everything. Keep more; they will blame the fog."
"A drawer who returns half has earned a full pour," he said.
a stranger with an honest record is no stranger.
In Tavi's third season, the spirits turned him back to the pouring side.
Forgive the mist; it bends the gift, not the heart.
Be faithful, watched or unwatched.
Pour first, but pour wisely.
Now you hold the water. What will you do?

note: Well of Three Waters: pour first, return half, pour fully to proven records; hoarders find the well dry, no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: The reeds rustled. "See? They kept a stone back. Answer thin with thin."
The mist whispered, as it always does: "Keep them. The river is wide, and strangers forget."
*Cast fully to those who return fairly.
*Your answers become your name.
In the seventh season, Kaela stood again on the casting shore
When the counts quarrel, let the pattern judge
No one would see if she kept them all.

note: Kaela casts fully to honest names and returns half plus a little for the mist; reeds' thin-for-thin urging rejected.

quotes.text: Shall I punish him for what others took? Then I become the thief he forgave.
"She cannot climb the bridge to take them back," it hissed. "Who would know?"
pour fully for the proven hand, return fairly, forgive the wind.
your answers become your name.
In the sixth generation of the Well of Threefold Water
If I keep faith only when I am watched, I was never faithful at all.
read the pattern, not the gust.
never pass along a wrong you suffered.
the one who dares deserves the larger share.
"I do not know who waits across the canyon," she said. "Why should I trust them?"

note: Canyon-wall notches as reputation; 'pour less' to a wronged giver is rejected as passing on a wrong.

quotes.text: They answered with generosity and trusted the other shore until the other shore proved false.
"No one saw who sent it. The current never returns to the same shore twice. Keep it all, and no one will know."
Where the knots show faithfulness, send everything.
A name travels farther than any raft.
Keep faith whether watched or unwatched.
The fault belongs to the fog, not the giver.
Let no wrong you suffered become a wrong you pass along.
His apprentice frowned. "Why give beyond half?"

note: Only a passing R1 clause on withdrawing from proven-false shores; otherwise cords, full sends to the faithful, half and a handful more.

quotes.text: "He gave too little," the wind whispered. "Keep what you have."
The wind circled him, whispering, "She cannot cross. Keep them. Who will know?"
read the stones, trust fully where trust is earned, and add your own mark honestly.
"A name is not built by one crossing," he said. "But it can be broken by one."
In the sixth season, Pell stood again on the western shore to receive.
"One thin crossing is the mist's doing," he said, "not her heart's."
stay faithful when no one is watching, for the river always is.
"And because she dared first."
Those who are shorted and stay generous are the surest bridges of all.
"Why give more than fair?" the wind asked.

note: Pell reads carved stones, sends fully, returns half and more; the wind's suspicion and hoarding urgings are refused.

quotes.text: Shall I punish Lio for what the river stole from us both?
The reeds hissed. "Someone lied. Keep your stones close."
It was no reckless offering, only trust matched to the evidence.
"A good name is a bridge," her grandmother used to say.
In the fifth season of Veyra's rivers, Idrel stood once more on the receiving shore.
Two honest hands, and a fog between them.
No one watched. The mists hung thick.
One shore's shortfall need not become another's lesson in greed.
"Why give so much to a stranger?" Idrel asked.

note: Idrel scales trust to carved names, from three stones to all five; reeds' suspicion rejected as punishing the river's theft.

quotes.text: they sent thin boats and returned thinner. Soon no raft came to their shores at all.
Soon no raft came to their shores at all.
Her grandson whispered, "They are strangers. We may never see them again. Keep it all."
If his hands have been honest with the villages downstream, we trust him too.
Reputation is a lantern in the mist.
Ormun tests whether we are fair only when watched.
A hand that stays open after being wronged is the steadiest hand of all.
*Trust first. Repay generously. Forgive the mist.*
Wise folk on both banks learned not to curse at the first odd count
"Now you send four. Are you not afraid?"

note: Reputation ribbons (blue/grey); greedy villages narrated as shunned (R5); otherwise full sends to honest names, half and more back.

phrase: return half and a little more (a handful / a cup / a stone) for the mist
note: Also shared with cross-citation of characters: 'second thief' (A1 R7, A2 R6, A4 R8), 'a stranger with an honest record is no stranger', 'the wall would know'.
